links.outcome: AI vs radiologist bone age agreement across clinical indication subgroups
links.effect: Mean absolute difference was 4.1 ± 5.6 months for orthopedic, 6.6 ± 7.2 for genetic/neuroendocrine and 6.7 ± 6.3 for oncologic indications; all ICCs were > 0.9, with the best agreement in orthopedic cases.
links.quote: Novel to previous studies, the indication for imaging was considered, demonstrating that agreement between algorithm output and radiologists' assessments varied across disease groups, with highest agreement observed in orthopedic indications.

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the performance and subgroup variability of an existing commercial AI tool (BoneAge) compared with routine radiologist assessments across different pediatric disease categories, but does not test an organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
